support.quote: Jean-Paul Sartre, awarded the 1964 Nobel Prize in Literature, declined the prize because he had consistently declined all official honours.

assessments.note: Same page: Pasternak (1958) 'was later coerced by the authorities of the Soviet Union' to decline — so Sartre is the only voluntary refusal of the literature prize (still true after the 2026 award to Anne Carson)

support.quote: Jean-Paul Sartre declined the Nobel Prize.
In October 1964, Sartre was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature, but he declined it. He was the first Nobel laureate to voluntarily decline the prize
In 1945, after the war, when I was offered the Legion of Honor, I refused it, although I was sympathetic to the government.

assessments.note: Sartre's own statement of 22 Oct 1964

support.quote: Il avait de même refusé la Légion d'honneur, en 1945, ou encore une chaire au Collège de France.

In 1945, after the war, when I was offered the Legion of Honor, I refused it, although I was sympathetic to the government. Similarly, I have never sought to enter the Collège de France, as several of my friends suggested.

assessments.note: Old body said the Fourth Republic offered the Legion of Honour 'for his role in the Resistance' and that he 'turned down a chair at the Collège de France'; in 1945 the Fourth Republic did not yet exist (Provisional Government), and Sartre says he never sought the chair. Body corrected.
